draft.title: Health as dynamic and subjective
card: Health is not fixed. It changes over time, from day to day and across a lifetime, as a person's body, habits and life change.
Health looks different from person to person. How healthy someone feels depends on their own values, goals and situation.
Two people with the same condition may rate their health differently. One may focus on what they can still do, and the other on what they can no longer do.
So a health check at one moment, or a single measure, does not tell the whole story of a person's health.
draft.remember: Health moves over time, and each person judges it through their own values and situation.

a.q: Which example best shows that health is dynamic?
opts: Sam felt very fit in summer but was run down after illness
Sam and Priya rate their own fitness differently
Sam values sport more than Priya does
Sam's doctor measured his blood pressure once
a.why: Sam's health changed over time, which is what dynamic means. The second option shows a difference between two people at one time, which is subjectivity, not change.
a.clue: Look for health that changes as time passes.

b.q: Leila and Tom both use a wheelchair. Leila says she feels very healthy because she plays basketball and has good friends. Tom says he feels unhealthy because he cannot do all the things he used to. What does this show?
opts: Health is subjective, shaped by values and situation
Health is dynamic, as Leila and Tom stay the same
Health is fixed, as a condition sets how healthy one is
Health is objective, as one condition gives one result
b.why: The same situation leads to different views of health because each person has different values and circumstances. That is subjectivity. The dynamic option is tempting, but the case compares two people, not one person changing over time.
b.clue: Same condition, two different views of health.

a.best: Sam felt very fit in summer but was run down after illness

b.best: Health is subjective, shaped by values and situation

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with a time detail ('in summer' … 'after illness'). A student could pick it without knowing the idea.

The why says 'the same situation' leads to different views 'because each person has different values and circumstances'. This contradicts itself and the card, which says situation is one of the things that shapes how healthy someone feels. Leila and Tom share a condition, not a situation. It should say 'the same condition'.

The distractor 'Health is dynamic, as Leila and Tom stay the same' contradicts itself, so it is too easy to rule out. Tom's 'cannot do all the things he used to' also hints at change over time, which muddies the contrast slightly.

opts: Sam felt fit in March but was run down by June
Sam and Priya rated their fitness differently in June
Sam valued sport more than Priya did in March
Sam's doctor checked his blood pressure once in June

a.clue: Look for one person whose health changes as time passes.

b.q: Leila and Tom both use a wheelchair. Leila feels very healthy because she plays basketball and has good friends. Tom feels unhealthy because he most values bushwalking, which he finds hard to do. What does this show?
opts: Health is subjective, shaped by values and situation
Health is dynamic, as their health changes over time
Health is fixed, as a condition sets how healthy one is
Health is objective, as one condition gives one result
b.why: Leila and Tom share the same condition, yet they rate their health differently because they hold different values and are in different situations. That is subjectivity. The dynamic option is tempting, but the case compares two people at one time, not one person changing over time.
b.clue: Same condition, two different views of health.
